prompt: Close-up of a generous family-style serving for four: tender braised pork in creamy paprika sauce with a large batch of boiled flour dumplings. Abundant pork shoulder pieces, cut as 2.5 cm cubes and now slightly irregular, are opaque and tender, with tan-brown seared patches showing through the glossy sauce. A large quantity of collapsed pale-golden onion wedges and strands is partly melted into it, while a smaller quantity of skin-on diamond-cut red peppers remains soft but recognisable and vividly red. Tomato paste, hot paprika and sour cream give the lightly starch-thickened sauce a velvety orange-red colour and creamy highlights; it coats the meat and pools beneath it rather than becoming broth. Beside and partly nestled into the goulash sits a substantial heap of irregular spoon-cut dumplings from the egg-milk-flour dough, plump and cooked through, ivory-cream with moist, softly rough boiled surfaces. Everything is arranged together in one wide, shallow white serving bowl, with pork, peppers and dumplings clearly visible and a large serving spoon resting in the saucy side. Bright soft natural daylight, a 65-degree camera angle, crisp detail and true colours; abundant food fills nearly all the square frame, with the bowl edges slightly cropped. Subtle steam, a calm pale warm-wood background and a small natural linen edge complete the clean, unmarked, ungarnished setting.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 1 kg total, 0.25 kg per serving, supplied as 2.5 cm cubes; although it contracts during browning and braising, it remains the most abundant solid in the goulash.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Chunky, slightly irregular cubes, opaque and cooked through, with tender fibres and tan-brown seared patches still visible where the creamy sauce does not cover them; braised rather than crisp or rosy.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 400 g total, 100 g per serving; a substantial starting quantity that collapses and reduces considerably during frying and the long covered simmer.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Soft, translucent pale-golden onion wedges, curved layers and strands, some still recognisable and many partly melted into the sauce, with no raw white crunch.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 2 whole peppers total, 0.5 per serving; visibly less than the pork and onions, added later so the pieces soften without disappearing.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Recognisable diamond-shaped pieces with their skins still on, glossy deep red, supple and tender after 20–25 minutes of simmering, with softened edges but not browned or charred.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: Made in the goulash with 600 ml of the 2.6 l total broth, 1 EL tomato paste, 1 TL hot paprika powder, Kümmel, 1 EL starch and 100 g Schmand; the remaining 2 l broth cooks the dumplings and is not served as extra soup. The starch and Schmand create a coating, lightly pooling sauce around the meat and vegetables.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Velvety and glossy, warm orange-red with creamy peach-brown highlights, lightly thickened rather than floury or watery, with onion strands and fine spice speckling throughout. The Schmand is fully stirred in, not a white dollop; any exposed bay leaf is a soft, whole, dark olive-brown leaf partly submerged in sauce.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 650 g flour total, 162.5 g per serving, with 3 eggs and 320 ml milk; this large dough batch makes dumplings a major component with a generous heap beside the goulash, not merely a small garnish. They plump as they simmer in broth until they float.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Numerous irregular, spoon-cut ovals and rough-edged dumpling shapes of naturally varying size, plump and cooked through, ivory to pale cream, with moist, slightly glossy yet soft-looking surfaces and a tender, fine interior texture; entirely boiled and unbrowned.

recipe_result: The finished dish is a generous family-style serving for four of tender seared-and-braised pork shoulder cubes with softened onions and red pepper in a lightly thickened creamy paprika sauce, arranged with a large batch of soft, spoon-cut boiled flour dumplings.
ingredient_context: Zwiebeln: 400 g total; 100 g per serving; rote Paprikaschoten: 2 total; 0.5 per serving; Schweineschulter (2,5 cm große Würfel): 1 kg total; 0.25 kg per serving; Öl: 2 EL total; 0.5 EL per serving; Salz: quantity not specified; Pfeffer: quantity not specified; Tomatenmark: 1 EL total; 0.25 EL per serving; Fleischbrühe: 2.6 l total; 0.65 l per serving; Lorbeerblätter: 2 total; 0.5 per serving; scharfes Paprikapulver: 1 TL total; 0.25 TL per serving; Kümmelpulver: 1/2 TL total; per-serving quantity unavailable; Mehl: 650 g total; 162.5 g per serving; Eier: 3 total; 0.75 per serving; Milch: 320 ml total; 80 ml per serving; Muskatnuss: 1 Prise total; 0.25 Prise per serving; Speisestärke: 1 EL total; 0.25 EL per serving; Schmand: 100 g total; 25 g per serving; Chili: 1 Prise total; 0.25 Prise per serving
final_plating_from_recipe: After the goulash is thickened and finished with Schmand in step 2, step 3 arranges everything together. In a wide, shallow white family serving bowl, the saucy pork goulash forms the base, with its onion strands and red pepper pieces visible; the drained boiled dumplings sit generously alongside and partly nestled into it, while sauce pools around them without concealing every surface. There is no optional garnish, separate Schmand topping or salad, which is only suggested as an accompaniment.

recipe_instructions.instruction: Zwiebel abziehen, in Spalten schneiden. Paprika abbrausen, putzen, in Rauten schneiden. Fleisch abtupfen, in Öl anbraten. Salzen, pfeffern. Zwiebeln ca. 10 Min. mitbraten. Mark einrühren. 600 ml Brühe und Lorbeer zufügen. 45–55 Min. zugedeckt sanft köcheln. Paprikawürfel, -pulver und Kümmel untermengen. Zugedeckt 20–25 Min. köcheln lassen.

Mehl, Eier, Milch, 1 1⁄2 TL Salz, Pfeffer und Muskat verrühren. 2 l Brühe aufkochen. Mit einem Löffel Knödel aus dem Teig stechen, in die Brühe geben und köcheln, bis sie oben schwimmen. Stärke mit 3 EL kaltem Wasser verrühren. In das Gulasch rühren. 3 Min. kochen. Schmand einrühren. Mit Salz und Chili abschmecken. Alles anrichten. Evtl. garnieren. Dazu passt Salat.
